newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails seven for up to 17 years for smuggling.
newsitem.headline: China jails seven for up to 17 years for smuggling.

text.p: A court in eastern China has jailed seven officials and businessmen for up to 17 years for smuggling nearly 150 million yuan ($18 million) worth of goods into the country, the Procuratorial Daily said on Wednesday.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court in Jiangsu province convicted the defendants of forging documents and under-declaring the value of goods they imported between 1993 and 1995, the newspaper said.

Yan Xinwei, former director of the municipal Foreign Trade and Economic Commission and general manager of a trading firm owned by the commission, was jailed for 15 years for smuggling, embezzling and taking bribes, it said.
He reaped 129,100 yuan from the smuggling activities, embezzled 60,000 yuan and took 58,000 yuan in bribes, the newspaper said.
Co-defendant Chu Dongping, an official of the trading firm, was sentenced to 17 years in prison because he was unrepentant, it said. Ma Jianbo, a customs official, received 14 years.
The defendants smuggled telecommunications equipment, air-conditioner compressors, colour monitors and pagers, evading 46.25 million yuan in duties, the newspaper said.
It did not say where the smuggled goods originated, but many traffickers favour Hong Kong as a base to penetrate China's porous coastline.
China is fighting an uphill battle against the smuggling of cars, electronics and other goods that are subject to high import tariffs, but the country's long coastline has made enforcement difficult.
Corruption and bribery, virtually eliminated in the years after the communists took power in 1949, has bounced back in China in the wake of two decades of economic reforms.
